title: Diversity Contraction Across Substrates: A Boundary Law for Semantic Exhaustion
creator: Nobel Glas
description:
This paper models diversity as a balance between regeneration and pruning near low diversity. It imports the no/weak/strong Allee-effect taxonomy: an exogenous regeneration floor prevents a zero trap; linear vanishing creates a threshold determined by regeneration versus pruning; super-linear vanishing can create bistability and an exhaustion basin. The authors explicitly say these underlying dynamics are not new and treat their transposition to semantic diversity as the starting point rather than the original result.

The proposed contributions concern mediation. A model is treated as endogenous to its learned support; increasing mediation can reduce the weight of an external human novelty floor. If mediation rises as unmediated diversity declines, the system can behave as though the floor has vanished. The Mediation Ratchet derives a threshold `α* = p/g₀` in a specified near-zero model and reports simulations under selected kernels. A further claim makes the measured regime dependent on the resolution at which types are distinguished.

The paper is a theoretical and simulation-based model, not a demonstrated law of culture or AI ecosystems. Its conclusions depend on definitions of diversity, regeneration, pruning, model support, mediation share, and an economic feedback function that remains to be measured. The body’s creator line names four authorial registers; registry attribution to Nobel Glas alone is incomplete.

wiki_article:
**Diversity Contraction Across Substrates** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks, Rex Fraction, Nobel Glas, and Sen Kuro.

The paper asks when a system can recover diversity after it becomes sparse. It adapts ecological Allee-effect dynamics to a semantic setting: systems with an external source of novelty resist exhaustion, while systems whose regeneration disappears faster than pruning can enter a low-diversity trap.

Its principal proposed extension is the **Mediation Ratchet**. If reliance on model-mediated production increases as unmediated cultural diversity declines, an existing human novelty floor may become disconnected from the channels that reproduce meaning. A threshold is derived for one model and explored through simulation.

The paper treats the ecological dynamics as prior art and presents the semantic and mediation interpretation as a hypothesis. Empirical measurement of the feedback between mediation and diversity remains open.
